To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ability of older adults to understand speech in noise is impaired by a combination of factors, including reduced audibility, increased masking, increased susceptibility to the effects of reverberation, and increased susceptibility to cognitive factors such as attention and working memory.
older adults have more difficulty understanding speech in noisy backgrounds than younger adults, and that this difficulty is not due to a lack of effort.

older adults are more susceptible to the effects of noise on speech perception, and that the effect of age on speech perception is reduced when listeners are given a task to help them focus their attention on relevant information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the auditory and cognitive systems work together in the perception and comprehension of speech, and how these processes change as we grow older.
the effects of age-related hearing loss on the processing of spoken words.
the role of cognition in the perception of speech, and with the role of speech perception in cognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the auditory and cognitive factors interact, but that auditory factors are more important in the earlier stages of the speech processing system and cognitive factors are more important at the later stages.
age-related hearing loss is a multi-factorial problem, and that the most important factors are the auditory and cognitive ones.
age-related hearing loss is associated with changes in both the auditory and cognitive aspects and levels of processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of age-related hearing loss are not limited to auditory processes but extend to cognitive ones, and that the two sets of processes may be seen as mutually compensatory.
cognitive factors can play an important role in helping listeners to overcome age-related changes in auditory function.

aging is associated with an overall slowing of the processing of information in the auditory and cognitive systems, and that the effects of such slowing are particularly evident when the demands on the system are high, as when processing speech in noisy conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auditory system is a very flexible and adaptable system, and the cognitive system is a very robust and resilient system.
the auditory system is not a passive conduit for sound, but an active, dynamic system that is constantly interacting with the cognitive system in order to make sense of the world.
